summary: Wartime-era wood-frame lookout building in Mariposa County on private land; built 1942 or 1943 (sources differ), used as an aircraft spotting station in WWII.

facts.design: 240 square foot wood-frame residence with 70 square foot cupola on a concrete foundation; Forest Service (Los Padres N.F.) design
facts.status_note: Register says standing as of May 2018. No later condition record was found.
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Madera-Mariposa-Merced Unit (Cal Fire MMU)

access.note: On private property; the register says there is no public access to the site any longer.

events.note: Clinton Preston, first lookout assigned, per the register; aircraft spotting station use in 1942 and 1943
Register gives early 1943; the same register page also says built in 1942 by Frank Greeley; fire-lookouts.org says early 1942
Used as an aircraft observation post and spotting station during the Second World War
Mid-2004: a communications company inquired about placing a cell phone tower on the site; last record in the sources
Register states the structure was standing as of May 2018
Registered October 22, 2019 with the National Historic Lookout Register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives early 1943 as the build date in one place and says built in 1942 by Frank Greeley in another; fire-lookouts.org says early 1942. The story gives 1943 as the register's date and mentions the 1942 accounts.
fire-lookouts.org gives GPS 37.1555, -119.5928 and a Raymond-area parcel; the register coordinates (used in the brief) are 37.265306, -119.991190. Not reconciled; story gives no coordinates.
Register says 1,380 feet; fire-lookouts.org says 1,374 feet. Minor; story does not state an elevation.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates match the register. fire-lookouts.org GPS and parcel description disagree and were not reconciled. Register text is partly garbled (e.g., steps removed 'on 1979'); not quoted. One WebSearch for a California Green Mountain found only Washington and Oregon sites, which were not used. Current condition rests on the register's May 2018 note; the fire-lookouts.org page was last updated 2013. No new photos.
